learningObjective: Precisely state the representable value ranges of INT8 (signed) and INT4 (signed) for symmetric quantization.
stem: For symmetric quantization to signed integers, which pair correctly gives the representable range of INT8 and INT4 (using the symmetric convention that restricts the value range to be symmetric around zero, i.e., [-127, 127] and [-7, 7])?

options.text: INT8 symmetric = [-128, 127]; INT4 symmetric = [-8, 7] (using the full two's-complement range).

explanation: Symmetric quantization intentionally sacrifices the negative extreme (-128 for INT8, -8 for INT4) to keep the range symmetric around zero, mapping the symmetric quantization scale to [-(2^(N-1)-1), 2^(N-1)-1]. This avoids the asymmetry problem that would otherwise complicate GEMM implementations. Option B is the unsigned range (UINT8/UINT4). Option C invents ranges (there is no +128 in INT8, no +8 in INT4). Option D describes the full two's-complement range but is not the symmetric convention used in quantization frameworks (which prefer symmetry).

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: +128 does not exist in signed INT8.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: unsigned range, not signed symmetric.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: standard symmetric quantization range definitions.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: describes full two's-complement, not the symmetric convention.

assumptions: Signed integer format with symmetric quantization convention.
The framework in question uses the standard TensorRT / PyTorch symmetric-range definition.
nonImplications: Does not imply the sacrificed value (-128 / -8) is never used; asymmetric quantization uses the full range but introduces a zero-point offset.
Does not imply symmetric is always preferred; asymmetric gives one more value at the cost of more complex GEMM.

distractorRationales.D: Describes full two's-complement, not symmetric convention.
